_why: One home for every version constraint in this suite. The templates and the canaries read this file rather than repeating a range, because a number written in two places is a number that will disagree with itself and no check will notice. tests/test_pins.py fails if any workflow hardcodes one. PUBLISH ORDER MATTERS: this manifest ships inside the wheel, so a floor naming a version that is not on the index yet is false for as long as that is true. Nothing here can check it -- that is a network question and this file deliberately asks none -- so publish every component a floor names BEFORE publishing this package. 0.1.0 shipped a manifest that was correct for ten minutes and cost a second release.

redfish-service-validator.role: DMTF's own schema conformance suite. Adopted, not built.

redfish-protocol-validator.role: DMTF's own protocol conformance suite. Adopted, not built.

bmc-sensor-audit.role: The referee: declaration diff, liveness, attestation. 0.2.0 is the floor and not a preference: from it the tool refuses `--insecure` beside `--pin-sha256` or `--cafile` rather than running unverified, and it answers `--version`. The coverage gate needs `validate-walk` and `capture --print-digest`, which is why 0.1.1 was the floor before the security fix raised it -- and this line still named 0.1.1 afterwards.

arbiter-engine.role: The invariant envelope the referee reasons with. The floor is DERIVED, not chosen: the referee's own Stage 2 canary fails 11 of its assertions on 0.1.6 and 2 on 0.1.7, and passes on 0.1.8. This manifest declared >=0.1.6 until 2026-08-24, so a reader pinning down for reproducibility would have got a referee that could not do its job, on the manifest's word that it could.

qa-orchestrator.role: Injects faults, drives captures, compares verdicts. 0.3.0 is the floor and not a preference: from it the harness is domain-free -- tiers, verbs, referees and report shapes come from registries, and the BMC tool with its tiers and scenarios is a vertical loaded through an entry point. `qa_orchestrator.backends` went with that change, and this pipeline read it until 2026-09-05. This line said 0.1.1 while the requirement already said 0.2.0: two records of one fact, drifted, which is what this manifest exists to prevent.

odm-cert-generator.role: Renders the certificate and holds unit identity. Published as `odm-cert-generator`; the command it installs is `cert-generator`, because PyPI refuses that as a distribution name. 0.2.0 is the floor and not a preference: the certificate records `walk_digest_verified` -- whether it COMPUTED the handle from the walk or was merely handed one and checked nothing -- and only from 0.2.0 is that claim worth anything, because 0.2.0 raised this tool own referee floor so a walk cannot have been captured by a command that asked to verify and not to verify at once. 0.1.2 is where `--walk` and `--walk-digest` arrived, which is why this line named it before the verification story raised the floor past it.
